ai_use_policy.value: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT do not currently satisfy our criteria for authorship. An attribution of authorship carries with it accountability for the Correspondence content, which cannot be effectively applied to LLMs. Use of an LLM should instead be properly documented in a footnote to the main text.

article_types.description: Brief comments on topical issues of public and political interest relating to research, or on magazine material published in Nature.
required_sections: Link to the Nature article under discussion

reference_limit.notes: Further citations can be included for fact-checking purposes.

author_limit.notes: Collective authorship designated as consortia, research programmes, societies, workshops or group initiatives is not permitted.

article_types.notes: Supplementary material is not permitted. Multiple affiliations cannot be published, so please highlight the preferred affiliation.

article_types.description: Entirely fictional, self-contained stories of around 850–950 words in length, focusing on 'hard' (scientific) science fiction.
article_types.notes: Unsolicited artwork is not considered. Prospective authors are advised to read earlier Futures stories at nature.com/futures.

article_types.description: Focus on one topical aspect of a field, providing a comprehensive literature survey. They can be controversial but should not be focused on the author's own work.
required_sections: 300-500 word outline of the background to the topic
article_types.reference_style: Highlighted references: for Review and Perspective articles, please write a single sentence, in bold text, beneath each of what you consider to be the most important or relevant 5 to 10 per cent of the references in your list, to explain the significance of the work.
required_statements: 300-500 word outline of the background to the topic
